newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rothfos trims world 96/97 coffee output estimate.
newsitem.headline: Rothfos trims world 96/97 coffee output estimate.

text.p: Global coffee output in 1996/97 is estimated at 97.0 million bags compared with 86.8 million in 1995/96 and down from a 97.5 million estimate in January, figures from German trader Bernhard Rothfos GmbH showed.

Rothfos said the estimate for Brazil's crop was raised by three million bags while Colombia's was cut by 1.8 million to 9.7 million and Indonesia's by 1.2 million to 6.3 million, apart from other adjustments.
The domestic consumption estimate in producer countries for 96/97 was unchanged from January at 24 million bags and compared with 22.6 million bags in 95/96.
Rothfos left its global 96/97 consumption figure at 99 million bags, made up of the 24 million in producer and 75 million in importing countries (versus an adjusted, identical, 75 million in 95/96).
The global exportable crop figure for 96/97 was lowered by 700,000 bags from January to 72.96 million (64.23 million 95/96), below the projected consumption in importing countries.
It said this demonstrated the present global deficit and the need for consumer countries to live off stocks.
